data.title: Contact dermatitis — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Contact dermatitis** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. Define contact dermatitis and its types.**
- Inflammatory skin reaction to external substances
- Irritant contact dermatitis (ICD, ~80%): non-immunological direct damage
- Allergic contact dermatitis (ACD): type IV delayed hypersensitivity to a hapten in a sensitised person
- Others: photoallergic, phototoxic, contact urticaria (immediate), protein contact dermatitis, systemic contact dermatitis (ingested allergen), airborne contact dermatitis

**Q2. Explain the pathomechanism of allergic contact dermatitis (PYQ).**
- Sensitisation (induction) phase — 10–15 days: hapten (<500 Da) penetrates, binds skin proteins (haptenation), taken up by Langerhans/dermal dendritic cells → migrate to lymph nodes → present to naive T cells → clonal expansion of hapten-specific memory T cells (Th1/Tc1, Th17)
- Elicitation phase — 24–72 h after re-exposure: memory T cells recognise the hapten-protein → release IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-17 → keratinocyte apoptosis, spongiosis, eczema
- Innate 'danger signals' (TLR, inflammasome) needed — explains why irritated skin sensitises more easily

**Q3. Differentiate irritant and allergic contact dermatitis (PYQ).**
- ICD: anyone exposed (dose-dependent), first exposure can react, onset minutes–hours, burning/stinging > itch, sharply limited to contact area, glazed/ fissured, patch test negative (or irritant), common on hands (wet work)
- ACD: only sensitised (minority), needs prior sensitisation, onset 24–72 h after exposure, itch, spreads beyond contact site/ id reactions, vesicular, patch test positive
- Histology overlaps; ICD more necrotic keratinocytes, ACD more spongiosis and eosinophils

**Q4. Discuss variants of irritant dermatitis (PYQ).**
- Acute irritant (chemical burn-like — acids, alkalis), acute delayed (benzalkonium, podophyllin, anthralin — 8–24 h later), irritant reaction (in wet workers), cumulative/chronic (commonest — repeated mild irritants: soaps, detergents, water), traumatic, pustular/acneiform (oils, metals), asteatotic, frictional, airborne irritant (dust, fibreglass)
- Subjective irritation (stinging without signs — lactic acid sting test)

**Q5. Name common contact allergens and sources (PYQ: list five common sensitisers).**
- Nickel (jewellery, belt buckles, jeans buttons, mobiles) — commonest in women
- Potassium dichromate/chromate (cement — construction workers; leather tanning) — commonest in Indian men
- Paraphenylenediamine (PPD — hair dye, black henna tattoos)
- Fragrances (fragrance mix I and II, balsam of Peru), preservatives (methylisothiazolinone, formaldehyde releasers, parabens)
- Rubber chemicals (thiuram mix, mercaptobenzothiazole, carba mix — gloves, footwear)
- Parthenium hysterophorus (sesquiterpene lactones — airborne contact dermatitis in India), Compositae, Primula, Toxicodendron (poison ivy)
- Topical medicaments (neomycin, benzocaine, ethylenediamine, corticosteroids such as budesonide, tixocortol pivalate), epoxy resin, colophony, cobalt, lanolin, kumkum (Sudan dyes, brilliant lake red)

**Q6. What is parthenium dermatitis? (important in India)**
- Airborne allergic contact dermatitis to sesquiterpene lactones of the weed Parthenium hysterophorus ('congress grass') in farmers; men > women
- Patterns: classical airborne (face, eyelids, V of neck, flexures, retro-auricular and sub-mental — not spared unlike photodermatitis), photosensitive lichenoid, chronic actinic dermatitis-like, mixed, exfoliative, prurigo nodularis-like
- Treatment: avoidance (difficult), topical/systemic steroids, azathioprine (weekly 300 mg pulse used in our protocol or daily), cyclosporine, methotrexate

**Q7. Differentiate airborne contact dermatitis from photodermatitis.**
- Airborne: upper eyelids, behind ears, submental area, nasolabial folds involved (allergen settles there)
- Photo: these shaded areas spared (Wilkinson's triangle behind the ear, submental, upper eyelids)

**Q8. Describe the patch test procedure.**
- Indications: suspected ACD, chronic/recurrent eczema of hands/face/feet, worsening on topical therapy, occupational dermatitis
- Allergens in standard concentration in petrolatum/water (Indian standard series ~20–25 allergens; plus cosmetic, vegetable, footwear, patient's own products) in Finn chambers on upper back
- Remove at 48 h (D2), read 30–60 min later and at D3/D4 (and D7 for late reactors — neomycin, corticosteroids, metals)
- Avoid: potent topical steroid on back for 1 week, oral prednisolone >20 mg/day, immunosuppressants, recent UV exposure, active eczema

**Q9. How do you grade patch test readings (ICDRG)?**
- – negative; ?+ doubtful (faint erythema); + weak (erythema, infiltration, possibly papules); ++ strong (erythema, infiltration, papules, vesicles); +++ extreme (spreading, bullous/ulcerative); IR irritant (patchy, glazed, follicular, pustular, sharply limited, decrescendo)
- Assess relevance: current, past, unknown, cross-reaction

**Q10. What are false positive and false negative patch tests?**
- False positive: irritant concentration, excited skin ('angry back' syndrome — multiple positive reactions when one strong reaction is present), pressure effect, impurities
- False negative: low concentration, poor occlusion, early reading only, steroid/UV, vehicle not releasing allergen, need for photo-patch or open/repeat open application test (ROAT)

**Q11. What are photo-patch tests?**
- Duplicate allergen sets applied; one irradiated with UVA 5 J/cm² at 24–48 h; reaction only at irradiated site = photoallergy (sunscreens, NSAIDs like ketoprofen, fragrances, chlorpromazine)

**Q12. What is systemic contact dermatitis?**
- Flare of previous ACD sites or generalised eczema after oral/IV exposure to the allergen — e.g. nickel in diet, balsam of Peru in spices, drugs (aminoglycosides after neomycin), baboon syndrome (SDRIFE — buttock/flexural symmetrical eruption)

**Q13. Write a note on contact urticaria (PYQ).**
- Wheal-and-flare at contact site within 30–60 min
- Non-immunological (commonest — benzoic/sorbic acid, cinnamal, nettles, cobalt), immunological (IgE — latex, foods; risk of anaphylaxis), unknown mechanism (ammonium persulphate)
- Tests: open test, prick test, RAST; protein contact dermatitis in food handlers (chronic hand eczema with urticarial flares)

**Q14. Classify occupational dermatoses (PYQ).**
- Contact dermatitis (commonest ~90%) — irritant > allergic; contact urticaria
- Infections (milker's nodules, orf, erysipeloid, swimming-pool granuloma), oil acne/chloracne, pigmentary (vitiligo from phenols/hydroquinone monobenzyl ether — occupational leucoderma), skin cancers (arsenic, tar, UV), mechanical (callosities, occupational marks), sclerodermatous (vinyl chloride, silica), nail disorders
- Mathias criteria for causation (7 questions — consistent clinical, exposure, timing, distribution, non-occupational causes excluded, improvement away from work, patch/provocation test)

**Q15. What is chloracne? (PYQ)**
- Acneiform eruption from halogenated aromatic hydrocarbons (dioxins, PCBs, PCNs) — many comedones and straw-coloured cysts on malar/retro-auricular areas, axillae, scrotum; marker of systemic toxicity; very persistent

**Q16. Management of contact dermatitis.**
- Identify and avoid allergen/irritant; substitutes (nickel-free, PPD-free dyes, vinyl/nitrile gloves for rubber allergy); patient information leaflet with names and sources
- Acute: wet compresses (Burow's solution), potent topical steroid, oral antihistamine; severe/widespread: short oral prednisolone
- Chronic: emollients, barrier creams (limited value), protective gloves with cotton liners, workplace modification; tacrolimus; phototherapy; azathioprine/methotrexate/cyclosporine for chronic airborne; alitretinoin for chronic hand eczema
- Nickel: dimethylglyoxime test to detect nickel release; EU Nickel Directive

**Q17. What is the dimethylglyoxime test?**
- 1% dimethylglyoxime + 10% ammonia rubbed on a metal object — pink colour means nickel release >0.5 µg/cm²/week

**Q18. What is chronic actinic dermatitis? (PYQ)**
- Persistent photosensitive eczema of sun-exposed skin in elderly men (often with parthenium/ Compositae or fragrance allergy), lichenified plaques, sparing of shaded sites; reduced MED to UVB ± UVA/visible; may mimic lymphoma (actinic reticuloid)
- Treatment: strict photoprotection, allergen avoidance, topical steroids/tacrolimus, azathioprine, cyclosporine, low-dose PUVA/NB-UVB (hardening)

## Quick spotter facts
- Cement + men + hand eczema — chromate ACD
- Hair-dye — PPD
- Eyelids, behind ears, submental involved — airborne (parthenium) not photodermatitis

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Contact dermatitis, occupational dermatoses); Indian standard patch test series. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
